sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Why the work unit is a closed list
sections.what: Explains that the work unit is a short fixed list of what one pass through a process handles. It is the label benchmarks join on, and the unspecified value is set on purpose when nothing fits.
sections.why: Stated in the docstring: free text fails silently, and retrofitting a list later would mean migrating stored runs.
sections.watch_out: Changing the list changes which processes can be compared, so treat additions as a real decision.

sections.name: WorkUnit (part 1)
sections.title: The fixed kinds of work
sections.what: Defines ten kinds of work (application, claim, order, case, invoice, transaction, shipment, program, incident, interaction) and an unspecified value, each with a plain description of what it covers.
sections.why: Stated in the docstring: keep the list small, and add a kind only when a real process cannot be joined to any existing one.
sections.watch_out: A process labelled unspecified is excluded from benchmark joins, so it gets no peers. That is intended.

sections.name: WorkUnit (part 2)
sections.title: Client wording lookup table
sections.what: A lookup table that turns many client phrasings into one fixed kind, such as loan application or drill program. Only listed phrasings match, and everything else is left alone rather than guessed.
sections.why: Stated in the docstring: an exact table is preferred to fuzzy matching because a wrong match is worse than no match.
sections.watch_out: New client wording needs a new entry, and a wrong entry silently places processes in the wrong benchmark group.

summary: Defines the fixed list of kinds of work a process can handle, plus a lookup table that maps many client wordings onto that list.
purpose: Give every process a standard label so processes can be matched for benchmarks. Without it, the same kind of work under different names would never match.
why: The docstrings say free text silently returns no benchmark peers, so the number looks computed when it was not. A fixed list makes the join key reliable.
how: 1) The file explains why the list is closed and why the unspecified value exists. 2) The WorkUnit enum defines ten kinds plus unspecified, each with a plain description. 3) The WORK_UNIT_ALIASES table maps listed client phrasings to a kind. Matching is exact, not fuzzy.
inputs: A client's own wording for the work, such as a loan application or a drill program.
outputs: One WorkUnit value. Unmatched wording is not guessed and should end as unspecified.
risks: Adding a kind or an alias changes which processes can be compared. A wrong alias puts a process in the wrong benchmark group, and the docstring gives a mining example. Exact matching means new client wording fails to match until someone adds it.
debug: If a process gets no benchmark peers, check whether its work unit is unspecified and whether its wording is in the alias table. Look at the raw label kept alongside it to see what the client actually wrote.
